android.desc:
Using Wero with your bank 
Wero is a European instant digital payment solution built by EPI and backed by major European banks.  
 
Customers of Deutsche Bank, La Banque Postale, norisbank and Postbank should download the Wero app and link their bank accounts directly to it. 
  
Customers of other participating banks can use Wero in their bank's own app. Availability and features depend on your bank and country of residence. Check your banking app to see if your bank supports Wero and how to get started. 
 
Once you have activated Wero, all you need is your smartphone to shop online and pay friends and family across Europe, instantly and securely. 
 
Key features 
•	Send and receive money instantly, 24/7, with just a phone number, email address or QR code – no need to enter long IBANs. 
•	Add as many accounts to Wero as you like 
•	Pay subscriptions and bills by scanning a QR code (Belgium and Luxembourg only) 
•	Split bills with friends 
•	Pay online at participating merchants (currently available in Germany) 

Easy setup 
•	Download the Wero app 
•	Link your bank account 
•	Add your phone number or email address 
•	Find friends who already use Wero 
•	You’re ready to send & receive money, shop online or set up a subscription payment. 
 
Send money 
•	Find a friend in your contact list, or enter their phone number or email address 
•	Enter the amount you’d like to send 
•	Confirm the payment and you’re done. They’ll get the money in seconds. 
 
Request money 
•	Send a payment request 
•	Show or scan a Wero QR code 
•	Set a fixed amount, or leave it open. 
 
Stay in the loop 
•	Turn on notifications to get updates on all Wero payments and requests  
•	Check your full payment history any time 
•	Get help from in-app support and FAQs whenever you need it 
 
Backed by European banks 
Wero works with major banks and financial institutions across Belgium, France, Germany and Luxembourg, with more countries and banks joining soon. 
 
What's next 
Wero is expanding, including new ways to pay in-store and online, and support for more European countries. In the fall of 2026 Wero will be released in Luxembourg supported by BGL BNP Paribas, Banque Internationale à Luxembourg (BIL), POST Luxembourg, Banque Raiffeisen and Spuerkeess (BCEE).

quotes.text:
iDEAL supports banks to implement payment in their online banking websites

So does Wero, as I cited in another comment:

The Wero app is available only for account holders from the German bank Postbank and the French bank La Banque Postale.

Are you a customer of another Wero-enabled bank? If so, you can easily use Wero within your banking app.

https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=eu.epicompany.wero.wallet

It's not the same system.

I said that it is based on the iDEAL system:

Wero is built on the foundation of iDEAL, backed by 16 major European banks – including the Dutch banks behind iDEAL. 

https://ideal.nl/en/naar-wero

The European Payments Initiative (EPI) acquired the Dutch payment system iDEAL with the aim of making it the standard payment solution across all European countries. [...] The first step is to make iDEAL the standard in France and Germany because the countries don’t yet have a standard payment system for e-commerce, according to AD. Customers in the Netherlands will notice little of this.

https://nltimes.nl/2023/04/25/dutch-payment-processor-ideal-become-european-standard / https://www.ad.nl/economie/online-betalingssysteem-ideal-wordt-basis-voor-europese-betaalmethode~a038bb73/

quotes.text:
If Wero is going to be similar to iDEAL, which it is based on, the payment flow will be through your bank's app. Heck, even the Wero app description says so:

The Wero app is available only for account holders from the German bank Postbank and the French bank La Banque Postale.

Are you a customer of another Wero-enabled bank? If so, you can easily use Wero within your banking app.

https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=eu.epicompany.wero.wallet

I have seen quite some people downloading their banking apps through the Aurora store (admittedly, it's a frontend for the Play Store, but you don't need an account or the app). Or you can use something like APKMirror and verify that they have the correct signing keys.

Of course, if they need Play Services or Play Integrity basic, then you need sandboxed Google Play or microG. If your bank does remote attestation through Play Integrity, then it is game over, but it is worth contacting your bank. E.g. some banks have added the GrapheneOS signing keys and added support for AOSP remote attestation.
